objective: Discover protein-protein interactions, pathway memberships, and genetic interactions for enriched genes related to doxorubicin toxicity vs efficacy in NF1 patients
methodology: Queried WikiPathways for pathway memberships, BioGRID for genetic/physical interactions. STRING PPI queries failed due to API parameter issues.

key_physical_interactions.significance: Direct RAS-GAP interaction; NF1 negatively regulates HRAS signaling
NF1 negatively regulates KRAS; KRAS hyperactivation implicated in NF1-associated tumors
Third RAS isoform regulated by NF1
Both involved in DNA damage response and tumor suppression; co-occur in cancer pathways
EGFR activates RAS pathway; NF1 modulates EGFR downstream signaling
RAF1 is downstream of RAS; NF1 indirectly regulates via RAS inhibition
PI3K/AKT pathway crosswalk with RAS/MAPK signaling
Both are tumor suppressors; genetic interaction suggests synthetic viability

key_genetic_interactions.significance: CRITICAL: KRAS and NF1 show synthetic lethal interaction - suggests dual targeting opportunity
Topoisomerase I synthetic lethality with NF1 deficiency
CRITICAL: TOP2A (anti-tumor target) shows synthetic lethality with NF1 - supports doxorubicin efficacy in NF1 context
Third topoisomerase with synthetic lethal relationship to NF1
EGFR inhibition may compensate for NF1 loss

pathways.note: TOP2B not found in WikiPathways - likely due to pathway database focus on signaling over enzymatic mechanisms. TOP2B is well-documented as doxorubicin cardiotoxicity mediator in literature.

candidate_targets.rationale: Central DNA damage response kinase; activates TP53; appears in WP2516, WP3878 pathways; potential synthetic lethal target with NF1
candidate_targets.mechanism: ATM phosphorylates TP53 in response to DSBs induced by TOP2A; modulating ATM may affect efficacy vs toxicity balance

candidate_targets.rationale: Parallel DNA damage response kinase; mentioned in WP1530, WP4016; responds to replication stress
candidate_targets.mechanism: ATR activation may compensate for TOP2A inhibition; ATR inhibitors could synergize with doxorubicin

candidate_targets.rationale: NRF2 transcription factor; master regulator of antioxidant response including GSTP1, SOD2
candidate_targets.mechanism: NRF2 activators could upregulate protective antioxidant enzymes to reduce cardiotoxicity without affecting TOP2A-mediated tumor killing

candidate_targets.rationale: Negative regulator of NRF2; KEAP1 inhibition releases NRF2 for antioxidant gene transcription
candidate_targets.mechanism: KEAP1 inhibitors (e.g., dimethyl fumarate) could boost cardioprotective antioxidants

candidate_targets.rationale: ERK2 kinase downstream of RAS/NF1; central to WP382 MAPK signaling
candidate_targets.mechanism: MAPK inhibition in NF1-deficient cells could reduce RAS-driven proliferation; MEK inhibitors (trametinib) already used in NF1 neurofibromas

candidate_targets.rationale: ERK1 kinase; parallel to MAPK1 in MAPK cascade
candidate_targets.mechanism: Dual ERK1/2 inhibition may be necessary for full efficacy in RAS-driven tumors

candidate_targets.rationale: MAP2K1; direct upstream activator of ERK1/2; NF1 pathway node
candidate_targets.mechanism: MEK inhibitors clinically validated in NF1-associated tumors; could enhance doxorubicin efficacy

candidate_targets.rationale: MAP2K2; parallel MEK isoform
candidate_targets.mechanism: Dual MEK1/2 inhibition standard approach

candidate_targets.rationale: RAF isoform downstream of RAS; frequently mutated in cancer
candidate_targets.mechanism: BRAF V600E inhibitors (vemurafenib) could synergize in BRAF-mutant tumors; less relevant in NF1-driven RAS hyperactivation

candidate_targets.rationale: C-RAF isoform; interacts with NF1 (BioGRID FRET data)
candidate_targets.mechanism: Pan-RAF inhibitors may be needed in NF1 context

candidate_targets.rationale: PI3K pathway parallels MAPK; both activated by RAS; crosstalk with NF1/PTEN
candidate_targets.mechanism: Dual MAPK + PI3K inhibition may overcome resistance in NF1-deficient tumors

candidate_targets.rationale: Downstream of PI3K; interacts with NF1 (BioGRID FRET); survival signaling
candidate_targets.mechanism: AKT inhibitors could enhance doxorubicin-induced apoptosis

candidate_targets.rationale: Downstream of PI3K/AKT; regulates metabolism and autophagy
candidate_targets.mechanism: mTOR inhibitors (rapamycin analogs) may synergize with doxorubicin; autophagy modulation affects toxicity

candidate_targets.rationale: PXR nuclear receptor; upregulates ABCB1 causing doxorubicin resistance
candidate_targets.mechanism: PXR antagonists could reduce ABCB1-mediated drug efflux, increasing tumor doxorubicin exposure

candidate_targets.rationale: CAR nuclear receptor; also upregulates ABCB1
candidate_targets.mechanism: CAR inverse agonists could prevent adaptive ABCB1 upregulation

candidate_targets.rationale: Topoisomerase I; synthetic lethal with NF1 (BioGRID genetic interaction)
candidate_targets.mechanism: TOP1 inhibitors (irinotecan, topotecan) may synergize with TOP2A targeting in NF1 tumors

candidate_targets.rationale: DNA repair enzyme; synthetic lethal with HR-deficient tumors; NF1 impairs DNA repair
candidate_targets.mechanism: PARP inhibitors could exploit NF1-associated DNA repair defects; synergy with doxorubicin-induced DSBs

candidate_targets.rationale: Cell cycle checkpoint kinase downstream of ATR
candidate_targets.mechanism: CHK1 inhibitors force mitotic entry with damaged DNA, enhancing doxorubicin lethality in tumors

candidate_targets.rationale: Cell cycle checkpoint kinase downstream of ATM
candidate_targets.mechanism: CHK2 inhibition may sensitize to doxorubicin; must avoid excessive cardiotoxicity

candidate_targets.rationale: TP53 negative regulator; MDM2 inhibition restores TP53 function
candidate_targets.mechanism: MDM2 inhibitors (nutlins) could enhance TP53-mediated apoptosis in tumors with wild-type TP53

candidate_targets.rationale: Anti-apoptotic protein; overexpression causes chemoresistance
candidate_targets.mechanism: BCL2 inhibitors (venetoclax) could overcome apoptosis resistance; synergy with doxorubicin

candidate_targets.rationale: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase; ferroptosis regulator linked to WP4313
candidate_targets.mechanism: DHODH in mitochondrial ferroptosis pathway; modulation could affect doxorubicin cardiotoxicity (iron-dependent)

toxicity_mechanisms.primary: TOP2B-mediated DNA damage in cardiomyocytes → persistent DSBs → cell death
secondary: CBR1/CBR3-mediated conversion of doxorubicin to cardiotoxic doxorubicinol metabolite
ROS generation → oxidative damage (mitigated by SOD2, GSTP1)
protective_pathways: ABCB1 drug efflux (protective in heart, detrimental in tumors)

efficacy_mechanisms.primary: TOP2A-mediated DNA damage in tumor cells → apoptosis
secondary: TP53 activation → cell cycle arrest and apoptosis
RAS/MAPK hyperactivation in NF1-deficient tumors → increased proliferation and TOP2A expression

therapeutic_window_opportunities.approach: Cardioprotection via NRF2 activation (upregulates SOD2, GSTP1) without affecting tumor TOP2A activity
Combine doxorubicin with MEK/ERK inhibitors to target hyperactive RAS/MAPK signaling
Combine TOP2A targeting (doxorubicin) with TOP1 inhibitors or PARP inhibitors in NF1-deficient tumors
Inhibit ABCB1-mediated drug efflux by blocking PXR/CAR upregulation
Develop TOP2A-selective inhibitors that spare TOP2B in cardiomyocytes

key_findings: NF1 shows synthetic lethality with TOP2A (PMID:27453043) - validates doxorubicin efficacy in NF1-deficient tumors
NF1 shows synthetic lethality with KRAS (PMID:19490893) - suggests combination MEK/ERK + doxorubicin
TP53 ferroptosis pathway (WP4313) links to iron-dependent doxorubicin cardiotoxicity
NRF2 pathway (WP2884) coordinates SOD2 and GSTP1 antioxidant response - cardioprotective target
ABCB1 regulated by PXR (WP2876) and CAR (WP2875) - resistance mechanism
NF1 physical interactions with HRAS, KRAS, NRAS (BioGRID) confirm RAS-GAP function
NF1 genetic interactions with PTEN, EGFR suggest PI3K/AKT pathway crosstalk
ATM/ATR DNA damage response pathways (WP2516, WP3878, WP4016) are druggable nodes for modulating efficacy
limitations: STRING PPI API calls failed due to parameter issues - WikiPathways and BioGRID data compensated
TOP2B not in WikiPathways database - cardiotoxicity mechanism well-documented in literature
BioGRID datasets very large (>2000 interactions for TP53) - sampled key interactions
No direct TOP2A-TOP2B interaction data - isoforms have distinct tissue expression patterns
Genetic interaction data from cell line screens may not fully reflect in vivo NF1 patient context
